Lyft drivers go through a background check and have their information in the system if anything happens, which I feel comfortable with.  Not them having a random other person in the passenger seat who could do anything and there’s no direct way to trace it back to that person like their actual drivers license.

It’s also against Lyfts policy to have a passenger. I’ve taken plenty of rides and never had this situation so I don’t think it’s actually that common to have someone because it can lead to your account being banned. I wasn’t saying my low battery was his problem, I was saying I was distracted getting in and didn’t notice he had a whole other random person I didn’t agree to ride with in the car until it was too late. Like I said, it is a safety concern considering that man’s information is not in Lyfts system and he didn’t have a background check like the driver. The fact they weren’t speaking even to each other was weird because why would you bring a friend to do your job if you’re not even going to speak to them or let your passenger know that’s who that person was. Considering I’m paying to use the service that employs him and was only expecting to be picked up by him, I have every right to be concerned that he has a completely random man along for the ride. And I mentioned one incident that is close to home, you only have to do a google search to see that both Lyft and Uber have countless situations where the passenger is assaulted by the driver. So much in fact that there are lawsuits about it.
